No, it is NOT normal for your abdomen to tear in half upwards during birth. That sounds like the plot of a sci fi movie. That doesn't happen. Your abdominal muscles can separate but it's not a tear; they are joined in the middle by a line of connective tissue, and that tissue can stretch due to pregnancy and not childbirth. It's called diastasis recti and it's something you can correct with exercise after having your baby. It doesn't cause pain or discomfort; it just makes your belly poochy until your muscles get strong again.

Your hips do not permanently dislocate during labour. Your hips have nothing to do with childbirth at all. Your body produces a hormone called relaxin during the last trimester which helps loosen up your ligaments and joints so that birth is easier - but that's all, just loosening,not dislocation. I've had three babies and not one bone has ever dislocated. That is not something that ever happens. Thank God, too, because yeah, dislocations are horrifically painful. My husband's destroyed a shoulder due to repeated dislocations, and even with a high pain tolerance he finds it almost unbearable. Don't worry about that.

C-sections aren't as bad as they used to be. The scar is small and low on your abdomen, low enough that it will be covered over by pubic hair once it's healed. And because they now cut the lower part of the uterus instead of the side or top, it is far less risky to have a vaginal delivery afterwards. Most women who have a section now go on to have what they call a VBAC - vaginal birth after caesarean. I'm one of them, so if you have any questions please don't hesitate to ask.
